section: Red flags: Fossil fuels, Fundación Repsol
before: Fundación Repsol is a corporate benefactor of Fundació MACBA and the funder of the Accessibility Programme since 2015.
after: Flag kept. Listed as corporate benefactor on Fundació MACBA page (copyright 2026, no year on the entry); Accessibility Programme since 2015 and 2019 contract for 41 works over 20 years (Fundación Repsol, 24 May 2019); statutes name Repsol, S.A. as founder; 2025 accounts record a 16,000,000 euro grant from Repsol, S.A.; Wikipedia: Repsol operates across oil and gas.
reason: Flag kept: a corporate foundation of an oil and gas company is a current benefactor (page copyright 2026; 20-year contract from 2019 still running; 2025 accounts show parent funding). The MACBA page itself carries no year for the entry, which is stated as the page copyright.

section: Red flags: Censorship of an artwork, 2015
before: ...cancelled the show the day before it opened, after curators refused to remove Ines Doujak's sculpture depicting former king Juan Carlos I. Three days later he reopened the show and resigned...
after: Marí asked the curators to remove the sculpture the day before the opening; when they refused he cancelled the show; three days later he reversed and resigned and fired Roma and Preciado (Hyperallergic, Claire Voon, 12 Nov 2015); ArtLeaks (19 Mar 2015) also attributes the decision to the director. Sculpture description cut; Queen Sofía point labelled Unverified with source; Marí's denial and his stated reason added.
reason: Flag kept: the space itself (its director) acted, which the House rules accept; no state body is named acting on the pages opened. The king depiction is not on the Hyperallergic page. Loan form date is as Hyperallergic gives it (28 February); Marí's account is attributed to El País as cited there. Artnet and Artforum pages could not be opened (403/402).

section: Red flags: Protest against the museum's expansion
before: A residents' platform ... opposes a plan that residents say takes about 1,000 square metres of Plaça dels Àngels for a new building.
after: Residents of the platform 'No to the extension of the MACBA' and skateboarders; about 100 people; they oppose the museum's expansion and criticised the city council's 'unilateral decision' to give the museum the space; council says it extends public space (El Nacional, Jordi Palmer, 20 Mar 2024). Ara (Antoni Ribas Tur, 9 Nov 2025): some thirty organisations oppose the expansion.
reason: Flag kept: the protest is aimed at the museum's own expansion and at the council (a consortium funder) for giving it the square, so it is aimed at the space and a funder. The platform's name targets the MACBA extension. 'For a new building' was not on the page and was cut.

before: Ministry of Culture (a member since 2008) / director said ... 'much greater emphasis' on companies / founding companies list
after: Ministry member since 2007 (MACBA history page); the unverifiable Ara paraphrase cut; founding companies (nine on the page, incl. Fundació Occident and Havas) and six corporate benefactors stated from the page; consortium funding text as on the history page.
reason: The Ara piece is partly paywalled; the corporate-emphasis line could not be read in full and was cut. Word count reduced from 989 to 784 by cutting peripheral overview and press detail; no heading dropped.

before: Esche said ... CIMAM's commitment ... was 'compromised'.
after: Esche's words quoted exactly: CIMAM's historic commitment 'was compromised by the position its president had taken in relation to Doujak's work'.
reason: Kept item: Hyperallergic, Claire Voon, 'Three Resign from International Museum Committee Board, Demand New Leadership', 12 November 2015; names MACBA and Marí.

section: Red flags: TD Bank guilty plea, 2024
before: TD is the largest corporate sponsor ... and funds a curatorial fellowship.
after: TD Ready Commitment is the largest corporate sponsor in the 2024-25 annual report, in the highest band at $200,000+, and the report names a 'TD Curatorial Fellow' post (summary statements dated 10 June 2025). Plea text kept: 10 Oct 2024, Newark federal court, about $3 billion (DOJ 1.8 bn, FinCEN 1.3 bn, Federal Reserve over 124 m), OCC asset cap (CNBC, Dan Mangan, 10 Oct 2024, on NBC News).
reason: Flag kept, same page types as Art Gallery of Nova Scotia (d048): sponsor page with a year (annual report 2024-25) plus a news report of the plea. The 'TD also pays for a named post' claim was reworded to what the report states (a post titled TD Curatorial Fellow).

before: The gallery's website carries the logos of the Saskatchewan Community Foundation, Canada Council ... / Fully wheelchair accessible, with accessible parking / $25 million anonymous donation endowed to the Saskatchewan Community Foundation
after: Funders now stated from the gallery history page: MacKenzie Operating Endowment at the South Saskatchewan Community Foundation, Canada Council for the Arts, Sask Lotteries Trust Fund for Sport, Culture and Recreation, City of Regina, University of Regina, SK Arts. Revenue figures confirmed: $5,827,575 total, operating grants $1,283,600, programming grants $432,793, fundraising $2,859,556, earned $959,343, other $292,283 (49 percent fundraising). Accessibility reduced to the plan-your-visit page. Donation: August 2018 (gallery site); C$25 million and 'largest in history' attributed to Wikipedia; foundation name corrected to South Saskatchewan Community Foundation. Bottom line no longer says the report names every sponsor.
reason: Logos on the site are identified only by image alt text and carry no stated funding relationship; the history page states the relationships in words. Annual-report text lists corporate bands exactly as in the report (it spells Committment).

before: Manege: public: the St Petersburg Committee for Culture, with corporate partners and sponsors / Committee for Culture ... among partners
after: Verdict: public institution working to a state assignment (report on the state assignment and plan for 2025 to 2027 on the official documents page). Committee for Culture: logo in header and footer and a name in the section 'cultural institutions and representations'; the pages do not call it founder or funder, so no funding line is claimed. Partnership page quoted as a listing: PhosAgro, Bank Saint Petersburg, VTB Bank, PSB Bank, Rosseti Lenenergo and others, with media partners; page says in general terms that partners help fund exhibitions, programmes and events.
reason: No flag: no entry has a year or amount, so none is a funding line; no sanctions flag claimed. Committee-as-funder claim not supported on any opened page (site, dp.ru, Cyclowiki). Bottom line now says the list names corporate partners without implying amounts.

before: riding hall of the Imperial Horse Guards regiment, which Empress Anna Ioannovna founded in 1730 / Pavel Prigara was director at the 2016 reopening
after: Riding hall designed by Quarenghi and finished in 1804; the Life Guards Horse Regiment was established by decree of Anna Ioannovna in 1730; reopened 25 June 2016; Prigara listed as director in a Sobaka.ru profile of 7 February 2017.
reason: dp.ru (16 February 2023, no byline) confirms Yalova as acting director from September 2022 and director from February 2023, announced by vice-governor Piotrovsky; it does not name Prigara.

before: Connection: Porsche Holding Salzburg, the MAK's partner from 2024, is wholly owned by Volkswagen AG (Wikipedia).
after: Kept in Wider context, no flag: RFA (Alim Seytoff and Roseanne Gerin, 27 Nov 2024) reports VW's sale of the Urumqi joint-venture plant with SAIC, the accusations of forced labour, VW's December 2023 audit and Zenz's judgement. Connection: Porsche Holding Salzburg, MAK partner since 2024 (annual report 2024; free-entry days 29 Dec 2024 and 28 Dec 2025), is owned by Volkswagen AG (Wikipedia: majority owner, infobox 100 percent).
reason: Porsche Holding Salzburg shown as a current partner: 2024 annual report (multi-year partnership begun 2024), MAK event page for 29 Dec 2024 and vienna.at, 22 Dec 2025. The RFA page does not mention the MAK or Porsche Holding Salzburg, so the point stays context only.

before: ...no security measures, no bag checks and no alarm, and that she saw no security staff for a long time. / highest security standards...
after: W24 (W24 Redaktion, 31 Aug 2026): witness to Die Presse online, 'keinerlei Sicherheitsvorkehrungen, keine Taschenkontrollen, nichts' (translated), asked why no alarm went off, called the museum's account 'beschönigend'; Hollein pointed to the highest security standards (to APA); ten security staff and cameras before the robbery; metal detectors and cloakroom now; detectors to stay at least until 27 Sep.
reason: 'Saw no security staff for a long time' is not in the article (staff did not appear until later is paraphrased out). Theft date 27 Aug 2026 from Wikipedia; W24 says only Thursday afternoon.

before: Free admission on MAK Day, Monday 26 October 2026, sponsored by Wiener Städtische. All floors ... accessible by lift / 'Glanzstücke'
after: MAK Day 2026 claim cut (no opened page supports it); accessibility reduced to what the visit page says (wheelchair-accessible lift; companions free); exhibition name cut; 'federal' dropped from the funding verdict: base funding (Basisabgeltung) 11,707 of 16,051 thousand euros confirmed in the 2024 annual report; Kuratorium list and sponsor thanks confirmed.
reason: MAK visit page does not mention MAK Day or Wiener Städtische. Wikipedia names the robbery date and necklace but not the exhibition title.

before: MAIIAM: self-funded: the founding family's private collection and money / opened on 3 July 2016 (museum website) / unsigned, '1342°C' (2020) ... the reason MAIELIE in Khon Kaen was designed to be more welcoming
after: Verdict: private, a collector initiative sharing the family's collection (ASEF Culture360, 17 Jun 2016). Opening date credited to ASEF only. Collection artists credited to ArtAsiaPacific as Booth's collection. Mirror facade credited to the museum's directions. Press item: ArtAsiaPacific, no byline, '1342°C', 1 May 2020 (May/June 2020 issue): MAIIAM 'with its gleaming facade, can be cold and intimidating for locals'; MAIELIE 'intended as a warm, welcoming place for workshops about art, culture, and politics'.
reason: Museum site gives no opening date and lists inconsistent opening days (stated as such). 'Khon Kaen' and 'to be more welcoming as the reason' were not on the opened page and were cut.

before: Cristiana Perrella became artistic director / Artribune describes the museum as municipal property / Soprintendenza declined to keep the 'Retrofuturo' works
after: Perrella named director (Finestre sull'Arte, 26 Mar 2025, Redazione). Ownership statements credited to Lo Pinto. Press item: Artribune, Livia Montagnoli, 'Luca Lo Pinto e il museo MACRO di Roma. Intervista di fine mandato al direttore uscente', 4 Oct 2024: lack of managerial and administrative continuity as the museum's 'tallone d'Achille', Palaexpo gave freedom, Soprintendenza did not accept the artists' proposal for long-term loan of 'Retrofuturo' works; acquisition budget reduced almost to nothing.
reason: Finestre calls her 'director'. The 'instrumental entity of the City of Rome' wording is on the Palaexpo page, not the manifesto page. Palaexpo board names confirmed on palaexpo.it.

before: chosen after a public call / the Region fully participates / partnership with Fondazione Morra Greco, where Forte had worked
after: Fabbris: examining committee, then board of directors (Finestre sull'Arte, 21 Jan 2023). Region founded the museum (arte.it). Press items kept: Il Sole 24 Ore, Maria Adelaide Marchesoni, 'Cercasi nuovo direttore per il Madre, troppo dipendente dai contributi pubblici', 13 Dec 2022 (3.4 m euros public contributions end 2021, 4.7 m expected 2022, 3.2 m operating costs 2021; fundraising activity not yet developed); Artribune, Giovanna Procaccini, 'Fondazione Donnaregina e Madre. Da otto a uno', 12 Dec 2012 (debts over 8 m reduced to just over 1 m; personalism question; Progetto XXI with Fondazione Morra Greco a no-cost collaboration).
reason: No public call is mentioned by Finestre. 'Where Forte had worked' is not on the Artribune page.

before: MAMbo: mainly public ... / No sponsors or amounts are named. / slightly under half of its revenue in 2020
after: Verdict 'mixed': the city transfer was slightly under half of Istituzione Bologna Musei revenue excluding staff costs (Balbi, Artribune, Santa Nastro, 12 Jan 2020). Absence sentence cut. Press item: Artribune, Redazione, 'Ecco come è successo che Gianfranco Maraniello è di nuovo direttore del Mambo. Anzi di tutti i Musei Bolognesi: a Vittorio Sgarbi piacendo. Storia travagliata di un rinnovo', 15 Sep 2013 (35 applicants, nine shortlisted; Lega Nord called the process rigged; Sgarbi its expert). Website line unchanged: https://www.museibologna.it/artemoderna/.
reason: Balbi's figure is for the whole institution, not MAMbo alone, and is from January 2020, so the bottom line now says so. Bread-shortage detail and 'largely accessible' were not on the opened pages and were cut.

before: Culture Committee chair Sylvia Björk quoted / Tuesday... Wednesday 11:00 to 19:00 / free guided tours and a free phone audioguide
after: Björk and the detailed hours and audioguide claims cut; Culture Director Elisabeth Lundgren credited with the city's reasons (Malmö stad, 12 Sep 2016). Konsthall part of Malmö stad's Kulturförvaltning confirmed on its site; Anshelm, 526 lanterns, 22 Mar 1975, directors list confirmed on the 50 years page.
reason: The 2016 city page names Lundgren, not Björk.

before: Marres: mainly public ... / The Friends of Marres page lists no members. / The Cultuurfonds collaborated with ... Werkhuis
after: Verdict: structural support from the ministry, the Province of Limburg and the Municipality of Maastricht (support page), plus project funds. 2022 income 1,149,687 euros against 1,011,818 expected, RAOCCC 30,000, municipal recovery fund 30,000, deficit 109,312 and 125,000 of released reserves confirmed in the 2022 annual report; Fonds 21, VSB fonds, KanunnikSalden, Sint Clemens, Mondriaan Fonds confirmed. Rubyfruit Jungle credited to Werkhuis, Cultuurfonds and volunteers (Marres site).
reason: No page states that public money is the majority, so 'mainly public' was replaced by 'publicly supported'. Free Friday evenings and the Elisabeth Strouven Fund confirmed on the front page.

before: 600-seat Sala Fernando Arrabal / called it a usurpation / Celia Mayer said companies at the Naves would be backed by a budget of 1.2 million euros
after: 'More than 600 seats' (brochure); sector reaction stated as an encroachment, with the headline's 'hostilidad del gremio escénico' (translated); funding model backed by a 1.2 million euro Madrid Destino budget for that season, so companies no longer depend on ticket sales (El Español, Alberto Ojeda, 7 Mar 2017).
reason: Kept item: El Español (El Cultural), Alberto Ojeda, 'Las artes vivas de Mateo Feijóo suscitan la hostilidad del gremio escénico', 7 March 2017.

after: Fillip (Ola El-Khalidi and Diala Khasawnih, Spring 2012) quoted as it reads: not-for-profit company; a participant's footnote about a grant; 'I am tired of fundraising'; LBC-Makan Restaurant pilot at the Congress of Collectives, other collectives bought shares, business plan unfeasible.
